result.title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement
result.summary: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. Furthermore, we extend LAPE to the setting with multi-view inputs through Cascade Feature Augmentation Fusion (CFAF). Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods can improve the calibration quality of various existing baselines and remain efficient and robust across different settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LAPE 后处理校准框架，以全局校准器输出为稳定锚点，利用特征空间中邻近校准样本的非参数局部证据逐样本细化预测，并通过 CFAF 扩展到多视图输入，在多个基线上提升校准质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「局部特征空间邻域证据 + 残差修正」思路，可能与 LVR 中基于置信度的 STOP 决策、证据加权聚合以及 latent 相似度检索的可靠性相关，可供核查是否适用于推理轨迹场景，但论文本身未涉及推理过程。
